name: TurboQuant and RotorQuant attention
plain: Per-model attention patches that change the numbers attention sees, then call the normal attention. TurboQuant rotates queries and keys by a seeded orthogonal matrix and rounds the keys (and, if asked, the values) to a few bits on a normal-distribution codebook. RotorQuant rotates channels in groups of three and keeps some of each group. Both run ordinary attention on the result, so they model the error of compressed attention rather than saving memory or time; RotorQuant keeping all three components is a pure rotation and changes nothing but rounding.
math:
TurboQuant: R orthogonal; q̃ = qR, k̃ = Q_b(kR) with scale ‖k‖/√d; out = attn(q̃, k̃, v).
RotorQuant: per triplet rotation r_g; keep the first k of 3 components of q, k, v; attention; rotate back.
